note: Election-day turnout as officials report it during the day. These are STATEMENTS to the press, not a feed - each carries the time it was given and who gave it. They move: Georgia's projection went from 1.2M to 1.4-1.5M between 1:30pm and 2:45pm ET. Only Georgia (statewide) and Harris County, Texas publish a running same-day count; no other state or county on this board does.

TX.source: Texas publishes no statewide running election-day count. Early vote 7.7M of 19M registered, per Houston Chronicle (Benjamin Wermund); 2018's early vote was about 4.9M, also roughly 40% of registered at the time.
TX.note: Early voting is normally 75-85% of Texas turnout, so 7.7M early implies a statewide total around 9.1-10.3M. Polls close 7pm CT.

TX:Harris.source: Harris County Clerk's office, via Houston Chronicle live updates (updated 4:59pm CT)
TX:Harris.early_note: 1,036,349 early in person plus about 45,000 mail. The Houston Chronicle's cumulative 1,224,000 minus the 143,000 cast today reconciles to the same figure.
TX:Harris.record_note: Harris broke its midterm record at about 1:15pm CT - 1,224,000 against 2018's 1,219,000 - and passed 1.3M by 4:30pm, a ~7% rise over 2018. Registration is up almost 17% from 2018, so the SHARE of registered voters turning out (46%) has not yet passed its own record.
TX:Harris.pace_note: Election-day pace is ACCELERATING, not fading: 19,111/hr to 1:15pm, 23,429/hr to 3:00pm, 24,000/hr to 4:30pm. Rain cleared mid-afternoon. At 24-30k/hr for the last 2.5 hours Harris lands near 280,000-295,000 election-day ballots.
